content.title: About
content.content: Bean soup is a hearty dish made from cooked beans, vegetables, spices, and sometimes meat. Beans are rich in protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates, making this soup a filling meal for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 7,000 years.
There are more than 700 bean varieties, differing in size, color, and flavor.
Bean soup appears in traditional dishes worldwide: Mexican chili, Russian bean stew, and Indian dal.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beans provide plant‑based protein that supports muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Bean soup raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beans contain flavonoids and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Raw beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and thorough cooking are recommended.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to legumes.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans contain oligosaccharides that can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve bean soup hot, often garnished with herbs, sour cream, or crusty bread. It can be prepared vegetarian with only vegetables, or with meat such as sausage, ham, or chicken.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in portion‑sized bags for up to 3 months.
